content.text: bisphosphonates inhibit osteoclasts; usually the drugs of choice for cancer-associated hypercalcemia; repeated IV bisphosphonates (bone mets, myeloma) are linked to ONJ; renal toxicity reported w zoledronic acid; oral bisphosphonates can maintain normal Ca but aren't generally used acutely; calcitonin (salmon) 4 to 8 IU/kg SC every 12 h; can ↓Ca by 1 to 2 mg/dL within a few hours; in cancer-associated hypercalcemia, limited by short action w tachyphylaxis (often after ~48 h) and no response in ≥ 40%. salmon calcitonin + prednisone may control Ca for months in some cancer pts.

CI: hypersensitivity to calcitonin salmon or any of the excipients (reactions incl anaphylaxis w/ death, bronchospasm, and swelling of the tongue or throat). Serious hypersensitivity reactions incl fatal anaphylaxis reported; consider skin testing b4 treatment in pts w/ suspected hypersensitivity to calcitonin salmon. Hypocalcemia w/ tetany (muscle cramps, twitching) and seizure activity reported; hypocalcemia must be corrected b4 initiating therapy. Meta-analysis of 21 trials suggests an ↑ risk of overall malignancies in calcitonin salmon-treated pts. Circulating antibodies to calcitonin salmon may develop and may cause loss of response to treatment. Concomitant lithium may ↓ plasma lithium concentrations (↑ urinary clearance); lithium dose may require adjustment. OD: hypocalcemic tetany could occur; keep parenteral calcium available for treatment. Most common adverse reactions: nausea w/ or w/o vomiting (10%), injection site inflammation (10%), and flushing of the face or hands (2% to 5%). Due to the possible association between malignancy and calcitonin salmon use, the need for continued therapy should be re-evaluated periodically.
